summary: Imperium: Legends is the standalone companion to Imperium: Classics, using the same card-driven civilization engine but with eight different, more fantastical factions (Arthurian, Atlantean, Egyptian, and others). It delivers the same tight asymmetric deck-pruning and clash-of-civilizations feel, and can be combined with Classics for even more variety.
praised: satisfying tableau and deck evolution over a short playtime
criticised: same fiddly keyword/icon lookups as Classics
combat can swing hard on card draw
requires owning or pairing with Classics to get full faction variety

interaction.kind: mostly parallel deck-building with a shared draft row, no dedicated Take That mechanic
interaction.detail: As with its sibling Imperium: Classics, players draft cards from a common row to build out their own civilization's deck and tableau, but Legends drops the explicit take-that raiding tag, meaning even less direct conflict. Nearly all decisions affect only your own engine; the shared row is the only thing players are racing over.

scoring.how_you_win: Same core system as Imperium: Classics with a different set of civilizations: build your deck by playing cards for icons/effects, and when the shared decks run out the player with the most VP from cards and completed objectives wins.
